import useOutlet / useOutletContext.description: Access the child route element and the context passed to it.

useOutlet().description:
The child route's element, or `null` when nothing matched.
Use it when the layout must inspect or wrap the child — animations, or an empty state when there is no child.

useOutletContext().description:
Reads the value a parent passed via `<Outlet context={...} />`.
A lighter alternative to React context for parent-to-child-route data.

import useInRouterContext.description: Check whether a router is present above this component.

useInRouterContext().description:
True when rendered inside a router.
For library components that must work with or without one.

useNavigate().description:
Returns a function that changes the location.
Prefer `<Link>` or `<Form>` where possible — they work without JS and are accessible by default.

navigate().description:
Go to a path. The plain form covers most cases.
Prefer `<Link>` when the user clicks something — it works without JS and is keyboard accessible.

navigate(), replace.description:
Replace the current history entry instead of pushing a new one.
Use it after login or a redirect, so Back does not return the user to the page they just left.

navigate(), with state.description:
Attach data to the history entry, read it with `useLocation().state`.
Not part of the URL — it is lost on reload and cannot be shared or bookmarked.

navigate(-1).description:
Go back one entry. Numbers move through history like `history.go(n)`.
There may be nothing to go back to (a fresh tab) — for a reliable "up" link use a real path.

navigate(), relative.description:
Navigate relative to the current route. `'route'` (default) walks the route hierarchy; `'path'` walks URL segments.
The two differ inside nested layouts — pick `'path'` when you mean the URL literally.

navigate(), viewTransition.description:
Wrap the navigation in `document.startViewTransition()`.
Pair with `useViewTransitionState()` to name the elements that should morph.

navigate(), keep scroll position.description: Skip resetting scroll to the top. For pagination, tab switches and filter changes where the user should stay put.

useNavigation().description:
Describes any navigation in flight: `state` is `'idle' | 'loading' | 'submitting'`, plus `location`, `formData` and `formMethod`.
The basis of global loading bars and pending UI.

useNavigation() busy flag.description: A single flag covering both loading and submitting.

useLocation().description:
The current `{ pathname, search, hash, state, key }`.
Re-renders the component on every navigation — read it only where you need it.

import useNavigationType.description: How the user arrived at this location.

useNavigationType().description: `'PUSH' | 'REPLACE' | 'POP'`. `POP` means back/forward — useful for deciding whether to restore scroll or animation state.

useBlocker().description:
Interrupts a client-side navigation so you can confirm it.
The blocker's `state` is `'unblocked' | 'blocked' | 'proceeding'`; call `blocker.proceed()` or `blocker.reset()`.
Only blocks in-app navigation — closing the tab needs `useBeforeUnload`.

useBlocker() with confirm UI.description: The unsaved-changes guard: block the navigation, then let the user confirm or cancel.

import useBeforeUnload.description: Run something before the document unloads.

useBeforeUnload().description:
Wraps the `beforeunload` event — covers closing the tab or a full reload, which `useBlocker` cannot.
Memoize the callback, or the listener is re-registered on every render.

import useViewTransitionState.description: Detect an active view transition to a given path.

useViewTransitionState().description:
True while a view transition to that path is running.
Use it to apply `viewTransitionName` to the element that should morph — pair with `<Link viewTransition>`.

import useHref.description: Resolve a `to` value into an href string.

useHref().description:
Resolves a `to` against the current location and basename, the way `<Link>` does internally.
Use it when rendering a plain `<a>` that must respect the router's basename.

import useResolvedPath.description: Resolve a relative `to` against the current location.

useResolvedPath().description: Returns the resolved `{ pathname, search, hash }` for a relative `to`.

useLinkClickHandler().description:
The click handler `<Link>` uses — honors modifier keys, target and replace.
For wrapping a design-system anchor while keeping correct link behavior.

import useParams.description: Read dynamic segments from the URL.

useParams().description:
Returns the dynamic segments of the matched path.
Values are `string | undefined` — even a required segment is optional to TypeScript. In Framework mode the `params` prop is precisely typed instead.

import useSearchParams.description: Read and write the query string.

useSearchParams().description:
`useState`-like access to the query string, backed by the URL.
`searchParams` is a `URLSearchParams`; setting it triggers a navigation.

useSearchParams() read.description: Read one parameter. `get()` returns `null` when absent, so supply a default.

useSearchParams() set.description:
Update one parameter while preserving the rest.
The functional form avoids clobbering params other components own. `replace: true` keeps filter tweaks out of history.

import useMatch.description: Match the current location against a pattern.

useMatch().description:
Returns the match (with params) when the current URL matches the pattern, otherwise `null`.
For active styling prefer `<NavLink>`, which handles it for you.

import useMatches.description: Read every matched route on the page.

useMatches().description:
All currently matched routes, each with `id`, `pathname`, `params`, `loaderData` and `handle`.
Combined with each route's `handle` export, this is how breadcrumbs are built.
The `data` field was removed in v8 — read `loaderData` instead.
